subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.

spec.name: Six-Wheeled Railgun Carrier
spec.description: A low-poly sci-fi military six-wheeled heavy carrier with a long electromagnetic railgun on its back, braced on four hydraulic stabiliser legs.
spec.layout: Long armoured 6x6 truck seen from the side: a wedge-nosed cab sits at the front (+Z) with a sloped glacis and a cyan-lit visor window. Behind it a long flat armoured chassis deck carries the railgun cradle. The railgun is a twin-rail barrel that points forward over the cab and extends past the nose, with a heavy breech block at the rear and a capacitor bank in a boxy housing behind the cab. Six big chunky wheels (three per side, axles at z=3.2, 0.2, -2.8) stand on the floor under wheel arches. Four stabiliser legs fold out sideways and down from the chassis at the front and rear corners, each with a hydraulic piston and a flat foot pad on the floor, slightly lifting no wheels. Hull is dark olive-grey with yellow hazard trim, white unit markings, orange warning stripes, and neon cyan energy accents on rails, capacitors and visor. All shapes are blocky and faceted, using chamfered boxes and low-sided cylinders.

parts.builds: Main armoured hull and frame from the cab back wall to the tail: a long chamfered lower tub (hull), upper deck plates (hullLight) with raised panel seams (hullDark), side skirts above the wheels, wheel arch cut-out frames in hullDark, yellow hazard trim stripes along the sill, orange warning chevrons at the tail, tail ramp plate with tow hooks and red tail lights, rear stabiliser mounting blocks at the mounts legBackL/legBackR (legRearL/legRearR), front mounting blocks at legFrontL/legFrontR, a thin white unit number panel and small rivet/bolt rows, exhaust stacks, and side equipment boxes. Everything rides joint body.
parts.attaches: Cab part starts at z=1.6 on cabFloor; railgun cradle sits on deckTop; axle hubs at axleFront/axleMid/axleRear lines poke out of the arches; stabiliser legs pivot at the leg mounts.

parts.builds: Front crew cab and nose: wedge-shaped armoured cab with sloped glacis (armor), angular side panels, a wide glass visor window (glass) with cyan neon inner trim (neonCyan), roof sensor mast with small dish and antenna, headlight clusters (white, trim) and bumper with a tow bar, front plough plate in hullDark with yellow hazard stripes, side doors with handles, mirrors, roof lights in orange, a roof hatch, armoured wheel-arch fenders over the front wheels, white unit marking, and a capacitor housing box behind the cab roof with cyan glowing coil bars. Rides body.
parts.attaches: Starts at the chassis front face z=1.6 at cabFloor; its roof is below the railgun barrel line (barrel passes above at y=2.3+) – keep the roof under y=2.0 near x=0 or leave the barrel clear by placing the cab roof at y<=2.0 on the centre; sensor mast stays off-centre at x=+-1.1.

parts.builds: Six large chunky wheels (radius 0.7, width 0.6) on three axles at axleFront/axleMid/axleRear, x=+-1.65. Each: low-poly 10-sided tire (tire) with raised tread blocks around the circumference (rubber), a steel rim disc (rim) with a dark hub cap, 6 lug bolts (steel), a small cyan hub light ring, plus axle housings, differentials and suspension arms (darkMetal, hydraulic) linking each wheel to the hull under the chassis. Each wheel rides its own wheel joint (wheelFL etc.) with the axis along x. Lowest tire points are at y=0.
parts.attaches: Wheel centres at y=0.7 on the axle mounts; suspension arms run into the chassis underside at y=0.9.

parts.builds: The railgun weapon: a cradle base with two side trunnion frames (armor, hullDark) at railgunPivot, a long barrel made of two parallel steel rails (steel) with a glowing cyan gap channel (neonCyan) between and cross-brace spacers every 0.5 m, a heavier tapered muzzle brake with yellow trim rings at muzzle (z=5.4), a big square breech block (armor, hullDark) at breechMount with a hatch and red warning light, a recoil piston pair (hydraulic) along the sides, capacitor coil rings (neonCyan, darkMetal) along the rear barrel, cable runs (darkMetal) to the capacitor housing, small ammo slug rack (steel) at the rear, and orange warning stripes. Barrel length about z=-3.4 to z=5.4 at y about 2.3, aimed forward. Rides joint railgun.
parts.attaches: Cradle base rests on deckTop (y=1.7) at x=0 near z=-0.6; breech at breechMount; barrel passes above the cab roof.

parts.builds: Four stabiliser legs deployed in the rest pose: each pivots at its leg mount on the chassis corner (legFrontL, legFrontR, legRearL, legRearR), with an upper strut running outward and down at 45 degrees (hull), a hydraulic cylinder with a chrome piston rod (hydraulic, steel) beside it, a vertical lower leg that ends in a wide flat octagonal foot pad (darkMetal) with yellow hazard edge and rubber bottom plate (rubber) resting on y=0, bracing gussets, bolts, a cyan status light on each knee and an orange warning stripe. Each leg extends to x=+-2.1 at the foot. Rides leg joints (legFL, legFR, legBL, legBR).
parts.attaches: Upper ends meet the chassis at the four leg mounts; feet touch the floor outside the wheels (x beyond 2.0) so they do not collide with the tires.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning the buildStabilisers function, using the provided Ctx type and designing each leg's stabiliser joint position and direction relative to its mount bone.

Now I'm checking for collisions between the foot pads and the wheels, since the rear leg's foot position at x=2.1 could overlap with the tire's radius at the contact height near z=-3.4. I'm adjusting the foot pad radius and center position to keep clearance from the tire geometry while still matching the spec's foot extent of roughly x=±2.1.

That still collides with the tire edge, so I'm shifting the rear foot further back in z, around -3.6 with a half-width of 0.28, which clears the tire with enough margin above the pad top. I'll keep the front foot centered near z=2.0 and work out the knee position for the strut geometry next.

Finishing the gusset triangle coordinates with thin offsets on either side of center, then switching the struts to use a boxed rod sweep for the frame geometry, and setting up a loop over the leg joint definitions to apply this to each leg.

Now I'm adding eight small dark steel bolt cylinders arrayed around the foot pad ring, writing the part-placement code using cylinder geometry with bone attachment, position, direction, and scale parameters.
